statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) through every remaining scheduled CME weekend halt hour and 9 to 13 (low) across the five reopen and Asian-session hours; Stress 25 (moderate) now, building to 47 (elevated) at the reopen; Confidence 59 (medium-low).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in the first nineteen hours covered here and Tail stays far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs from 25 to 47 as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence eases from 59 to 47 as the Friday reference tape ages before recovering to 67 once live price discovery would resume. No danger window is published, because no observed one-way structure exists and none can form while the venue is closed.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 31: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%) closed near the low of a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range, NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, with September hike odds around 57% after Jackson Hole; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC as the twentieth slot of this window
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which falls inside this window as its final five slots, so the first nineteen hours assessed here are a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. The reference tape was re-verified against primary sources this run and was unchanged: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close, finishing near the lower end of that range; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43, down 0.55 percent, within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year; Friday's own move was reported separately, with the 10-year closing near 4.72 percent, up about four basis points, and the policy-sensitive 2-year rising roughly twelve basis points to about 4.36 percent after Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks lifted the priced odds of a September increase to about 57 percent from roughly 35 percent the prior day. Crude closed slightly lower, WTI at 83.44 and Brent at 88.29, which does not corroborate a supply-driven shock despite an unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption in which shipping traffic remains well below normal and U.S. sanctions pressure continued over the weekend. Friday's session internals were split, with semiconductors broadly lower against firmer large-cap software and consumer names, a configuration that reduces directional conviction rather than establishing the persistent one-way structure Tail is defined against. The shared delayed cross-asset context file was stale at this assessment time, so this run rests entirely on independent verification from primary sources. Tail is therefore held at 5 for every remaining halt hour and published conditionally between 9 and 13 across the reopen and Asian-session slots; Stress builds from 25 to a 47 peak at the reopen as unpriced information accumulates ahead of a dense 1 to 4 September calendar that includes ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP and the Beige Book, Broadcom's fiscal Q3 results, ISM Services and the August employment report; Confidence decays to 47 on tape age before recovering to 67 once an open market could again be observed.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 03:00 UTC on Saturday 29 August to 02:00 UTC on Sunday 30 August, hours 7 to 30 of the CME weekend halt. The mode was normal in every slot and the mapped policy state never left EA_ON. Tail held the 5 floor in all twenty-four hours, because no venue was open to produce the price-path evidence Tail is defined against. Stress rose from a 22 trough through 23 and 24 to a 25 plateau held for the final twenty-one slots, while Confidence declined steadily from 82 to 60 as the Friday reference tape aged without any new observation to refresh it. No slot was unavailable and no assessment in the window was revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The first nineteen hours of this window fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; Tail is held at 5 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON, and the dominant mode is normal in those slots because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress climbs from 25 to 42 across those hours as unpriced weekend information accumulates against Friday's hawkish front-end repricing and the dense 1 to 4 September macro week, while Confidence decays from 59 to 47 purely through the ageing of the reference tape. The final five slots are the scheduled Globex reopen at 22:00 UTC, the first full hour after it, the hour around the Tokyo cash open and the established Asian session: they are the first hours in this window that can host observable structure and are published with conditional Tail readings of 13, 12, 11, 10 and 9, each of which keeps the mapped state at EA_ON. Stress peaks at 47 in the reopen hour and then eases as backlog clears into an open market, and Confidence recovers to 67. Those reopen readings are conditional scenarios; no post-reopen price path has been observed at this assessment time, and the actual structure will be scored in later runs.
